A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, core sections and experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training results, geometry-optimization success rates, molecular-dynamics trajectories, and fine-tuning and multiple-time-stepping experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds interaction-range experiments, heterogeneous-system simulations, stress-prediction tests, stabilization analyses and measured simulation timings.

M1.justification: v3 extends hybrid multiple time stepping to periodic conservative-stress corrections in constant-pressure dynamics (Appendix G.3). The PET architectures, conservative fine-tuning procedure and existing force-based MTS updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds molecular-dynamics evaluations of benzene on graphene, alanine dipeptide in water, and oxygen on a Sc-Co-Al alloy surface, plus NPH/NPT direct-stress tasks (Appendices G and I). OC20 training already appeared in v2; the adsorbate dynamics evaluation is new task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds PET-MAD comparisons involving conservative, direct and MTS stress treatments, and conservative versus velocity-rescaled direct-force dynamics (Appendices G.3–G.4). Earlier comparator membership is retained. The ORB-v2 wording is a clarification: v2 already specifies orb-v2.

E3.justification: New protocols include a two-versus-three-message-passing-layer comparison, constant-pressure tests holding forces conservative while varying stresses, stepwise velocity rescaling, and a specified high-pass GLE thermostat (Appendices C and G). These substantially expand the evaluation design; existing training splits, budgets and optimization criteria are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a receptive-range/depth ablation, controls isolating direct-stress errors, tests of velocity rescaling and GLE stabilization, and MTS stride/stability analysis for adsorbed oxygen. These examine several additional failure mechanisms and mitigation strategies beyond the retained v2 analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report parenthesized temperature uncertainties and structural-correlation bands spanning two standard errors. The new GLE table follows the existing reporting practice; v3 adds no reported seed counts, repeated-run counts or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables retain their numerical entries. New results include depth-dependent force errors (Table 3), GLE temperatures of 1181.5 K for ORB and 524.1 K for PET-NC (Table 9), stress/rescaling trajectories, and MTS-8 slowdowns of 1.19 for oxygen/alloy and 1.18 for water (Table 10). These are additional results under their stated conditions.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives the receptive-range difference between differentiated and directly predicted forces using three-body forms (Equations 10–11). Appendix I adds MTS cost expressions and computation-sharing assumptions. The original conservation criterion, harmonic-mode analysis and MTS update equations remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and Discussion retain the central warnings about non-conservative forces and the recommendation to combine conservative and direct-force predictions for reliable acceleration. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving receptive range and descriptor degeneracies, extends the discussion to stress/enthalpy conservation, explains why energy rescaling does not restore equipartition, and attributes the tested GLE's failure to insufficient damping of near-diffusive modes. These substantially broaden the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v3 specifies PET-MAD version 1.1 for stress tests, identifies the barostat and GLE parameters, and discloses that its MTS implementation does not reuse conservative/direct computations. A practical MTS example link supplements the existing Zenodo archive. Earlier software versions and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds discussion of Eissler et al., Loew et al. and Fu et al. concerning conservation, system size, phonons and downstream reliability. Additional citations support PET-MAD, velocity rescaling, interaction range and GLE analyses, while the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. Changes include local grammar and terminology edits, expanded explanations, inserted appendix subsections, updated cross-references, and reversal of the Acknowledgements/Impact Statement order.

P2.justification: v3 adds displays for interaction range, stress dynamics, velocity rescaling, GLE results and MTS timings/adsorbate dynamics. The materials plot expands from three to five panels. Retained displays are largely relocated or renumbered, with some axis, legend and caption edits; Figure 9 retains an outdated three-material caption.

improvement.justification: v2's MTS simulation evidence centered on water; v3 measures practical overhead and validates the approach for adsorbed oxygen and constant-pressure stress dynamics. Controlled stress tests and evaluations of rescaling/GLE remedies substantially strengthen the investigation of failure mechanisms, while Appendix C explains an additional architectural limitation. These gains materially improve the support and usefulness of the paper's recommendations, despite the outdated Figure 9 caption.
